about: Thinking out loud on a walk, as the iPhone would write it down: one voice (You), in segments of a few seconds cut at pauses, with Parakeet's punctuation and the ums left in. Written for the bench: no real people's names (Sam is the bench's generic name). Each expected item names the sentences it comes from by a phrase in them (`from`), what a good reading writes (`title`), and the agents that would be right for it (`agents`, the bench library's; `nobody` for none). `talking` is whether it should read as talking to someone. The `calls` are one voice talking to someone the iPhone can't hear. The two long walks (walk-13, walk-14) are two long walks of thinking out loud, written after the critics for the bench (no real people's names; Sam is the bench's generic name), in the schema of ../monologues.json: segments as the iPhone would write them down, one voice (You), Parakeet's punctuation and the ums left in. Each expected item names its sentences by a phrase in them (`from`), what a good reading writes (`title`, never an agent's name), the agents that would be right (`agents`, the bench library's; `nobody` for none), `named` when a name the user said decides, `mentioned` when an agent is named only tentatively (it restricts, never decides), and `handed`: whether Auto's rule should hand it over with the bench's agents set up as part 12.2's self-test has them (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, Inkwell take cards; Kestrel may act; Pennant checks the board). `moments` are sentences that went as moments of their own during the capture, left out of the reading. `negatives` must give no item: musing, things taken back or put off, other people's products and tasks, remarks.

monologues.about: a ten-minute walk to the harbour: a reply owed, an agent named, one named only tentatively, a complaint about someone else's app, an idea taken back, a topic come back to
segments: Okay. Walking down to the harbour now. So, a few things from this morning, while I still remember them.
It's cold for October. Nice, though, the light on the water.
Right. The board on the iPhone, when it comes back from the background, it takes like ten seconds before it shows anything.
That's way too slow. People will think it's broken, honestly. I thought it was broken the first time.
I wonder if it's loading everything again instead of just what changed. Probably.
Hmm. And the onboarding, the third screen, the button is half off the screen on the small iPhones.
I noticed that on the old phone this morning. It's cut off at the bottom, you can't even tap it.
Which is not great for the first thing people see.
Okay. What else. Oh, Sam asked about the booth for the fair, and I still haven't answered him.
I should get back to him today, before he books something else without me.
The wind's picking up. Should have brought the other jacket, really.
Okay, so, pricing. I keep going back and forth on the team plan.
Maybe it's per seat. Or maybe it's one flat price for a small team. I don't know yet, I'll think about it more.
Per seat is fairer. Flat is simpler to explain. Both have a point.
We could do a referral thing, like a month free if you bring a friend. No, actually, that's a bad idea, it makes it feel cheap. Forget that.
The ferry app keeps crashing when I try to buy a ticket, it's so annoying. Every single time.
Anyway. The release notes for the beta, I should write those this week, people keep asking what changed.
Inkwell could draft them from the changelog, actually. I might do that, I don't know.
And I need to email the accountant the receipts from September, that's overdue now.
Hmm. What was the other thing. There was another thing, I had it a minute ago.
Oh yes. Search on the Mac doesn't find anything in old captures. I searched for the venue yesterday and got nothing at all.
I should get Claude Code to look at that, it's probably the index.
Come on, light. This crossing takes forever.
Here's a thought: a little weekly email of what the agents did, with the cards they finished.
Something I could read on Sunday morning with a coffee. That would be nice.
People would like that too, I think. It shows the thing is working while you're not looking.
Seagulls everywhere today. They're loud.
Back to the onboarding. The third screen also still has the old logo, I'm pretty sure.
Yeah, it does. The purple one, from before.
Codex did a really nice job on the footer links, by the way. That's much better now.
I keep thinking about what to show at the fair. The board, obviously, we decided that already.
Sam's printing the banner, he said he would.
Okay. I think that's most of it. Nearly at the harbour.
Oh, and the dentist. I need to move Thursday's appointment, I can't make it then.
Right. Okay. Coffee.

monologues.about: a twenty-minute walk by the river: sixteen things, two moments said on their own inside it, "Hey Siri", other people's products, something taken back, something put off, a topic come back to, three names said and one said tentatively, and the musing between them that a long walk has
segments: Right, long walk today. Let's see what's on my mind.
Lovely morning. The path by the river is still muddy from all the rain.
I keep forgetting how nice it is out here in the mornings. Hardly anyone about.
The new shoes are good. Took a week to get used to them.
So, the export. The export from a binder doesn't include the dates on the to-dos, which is kind of the whole point of it.
I exported Website yesterday and none of the dates were in the file.
That needs fixing, soon.
Hmm. Somebody's walking three dogs at once over there. Impressive.
Funny, the board started as a list on a napkin. Now look at it.
There's that man with the kite again. Every Sunday.
It's funny, I think better when I'm walking. Something about not looking at a screen.
Okay, what else. The widget in dark mode, the text is way too dark to read, it's grey on almost black.
I could barely see it this morning in the kitchen.
The last two weeks went fast. The beta, the fair coming up, everything at once.
Hmm. Lost my thread. Where was I going with that.
It's getting warmer now the sun's up. Jacket off soon.
I owe the landlord an answer about renewing the lease. I said I'd tell him by the end of the month.
I should do that this week, it's already the twenty-fourth.
Ugh, and the airline's website logged me out twice while I was trying to change my seat. Unbelievable.
Not my problem, though. Moving on.
I liked the talk at the meetup last week. The one about small tools.
That was a good point she made, that people trust things they can see working.
Idea for the board: what if cards could snooze, like snooze until Monday, and then come back on their own.
That would be really handy for things I can't do yet.
So I don't have to look at them every single day.
Hey Siri, set a timer for twenty minutes.
Okay, the wind's dropped. Much better.
I wonder how many people actually read the changelog. Probably very few.
Okay. Where was I. The pricing page, there's a typo in the second paragraph, it says teh instead of the.
Someone pointed that out last week and it's still there.
Codex could fix that in a second, honestly.
The bank app is so slow these days. It takes forever to open.
Still, it's good to have it there.
The fair's going to be busy. Lots of people walking past, not stopping.
Anyway.
I need to book the car service for next week, it's been making that noise again.
Like a rattle when it's cold. Probably nothing, but still.
Two weeks is nothing, really. It'll come round fast.
That tree came down in the storm, look. Right across the path, they've cut it up.
I like the new icon, actually. It took a while, but it's right now.
Mm. Smells like rain, though.
I had a good chat with Sam yesterday. He's keen on the fair.
Okay, the newsletter. I want Inkwell to draft the October one, from the changelog and the blog posts.
And it should mention the new widget, lots of people asked about it.
Hmm. What's that bird. A heron, I think. Standing very still.
He always is, to be fair.
Okay, quiet bit. Just walking.
We should drop the free plan. Hmm. No. No, keep it, that's how people find us. Keep it.
There's a bakery smell from somewhere. That's dangerous.
I think the beta's going well, mostly. People seem to get it.
The upload, um, the thing with the upload. It just hangs, like, when the file is big. Over a hundred megs or so.
I saw it twice with the screen recordings.
So that needs looking at.
A few of them use it every day now, which is more than I expected.
Binders, remind me to call the bank tomorrow morning.
The numbers are small, but that's fine for now.
Okay. And I want Grok Bot to compare what the other notes apps charge for teams, for the pricing page.
Just the main five or six, and what you get for it.
That would help with the team plan decision.
The team plan, still not sure. Per seat feels fair, but it's more to explain.
I'll decide that next week, not now.
Hmm. A dog just ran off with someone's glove. Brilliant.
Ducks. Look at that, a whole line of them crossing.
The river's really high. The bench by the water is half under.
Right, where was I. The fair, the pricing, the export.
The search is fast now, by the way. Much better since the update.
It's a lot, but it's the good kind of a lot.
Oh. The share sheet on the iPad doesn't show Binders at all. It shows up on the iPhone, but not on the iPad.
I tried it with a photo and with a link, nothing.
That's a bug for sure.
My phone's at sixty percent. Fine.
And I should print the badges for the booth before Friday.
Sam's bringing the banner, I think. He said he would.
Last time I walked this far it rained the whole way.
I need to renew the domain, it lapses next month.
Okay. Hmm. Quiet stretch here.
The boats are out today. Sailing club, probably.
People keep saying the board is the best part. Which is nice to hear.
I like that the board shows who's on what. That part works.
What if the home page had a short film, like thirty seconds, showing a walk like this one turning into cards.
That could be really good, actually. Show, don't tell.
I'd need someone to film it, though. Or I just do it on the phone.
Hmm. Okay.
The onboarding, the second step, people get lost there. I watched two people try it and they both stopped.
They didn't see the button to go on, it's too low down.
There's the bridge. Halfway.
Nearly at the café. No, keep going, a bit further.
It's quieter on this side of the river. Fewer bikes.
It's nice not having anything in my ears for once.
Back to the export. It should also put the binder's name at the top of the file.
Otherwise you can't tell which binder it came from when you open it later.
Funny how the simplest things take the longest. That should have been a day's work.
Okay. Thinking.
The weather's turning, I think. Those clouds.
The pricing page itself looks fine otherwise, I think. Clean.
Oh, I should ask Codex what it changed in the sync code last week, the release notes need it.
Somebody waved at me. No idea who that was.
Right. Thinking about the fair again. Two weeks.
The booth is small, so maybe one screen and the phone. That's enough.
I wonder what Sam thinks about the team plan. I'll hear soon enough.
Ha. Probably from the gym.
The coffee place on the corner does a good flat white. Might stop there on the way back.
The sun's properly out now.
Hmm, the calendar on the Mac, the week view cuts off the last day, Sunday's just not there.
That's been like that since the last update, I think.
Anyway, no rush on any of this. One at a time.
My legs are tired. Long way still.
The swans are back. Two of them.
The light is changing. Everything goes orange at this hour.
Okay, nearly done. Heading back now.
Right. Nearly home now. That was a good walk.
Lots to do. Okay.
